summary: The main article describes a photoredox-catalyzed direct sulfonylation of anilines using sulfinate salts. It includes an optimization table for reaction conditions, a scope table for various anilines and sulfinate salts, a mechanistic scheme, and a derivatization scheme for the synthesized sulfones.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Biologically active sulfones, and the reaction targeted in this work.
items.description: Displays examples of biologically active sulfones like Vismodegib and Mesotrione alongside the general reaction scheme for the direct sulfonylation of anilines.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Selected optimization studies for the preparation of sulfone 1 a
items.description: This table details the screening of various photoredox catalysts, solvents, and additives to optimize the yield of the sulfonylation reaction.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Scope of the direct sulfonylation of aniline derivatives a
items.description: A comprehensive table showing the substrate scope for anilines, sulfinate salts, and the late-stage functionalization of drug compounds like Linezolid and Promethazine.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: A plausible reaction mechanism for photoredox mediated aryl sulfonylation showing the iridium ion enabled oxidative quenching cycle.
items.description: Illustrates the proposed catalytic cycle involving the oxidation of aniline and sulfinate salts via an iridium-based photoredox catalyst.
